strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 4 QA datasets (NQ, TriviaQA, HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA) with diverse baselines including RECOMP and NoiseFilter-IB
Pragmatic solution to supervision problem by using downstream task performance as reward signal, avoiding need for expensive compression labels
Strong and consistent empirical results: achieves 3-6% token compression while maintaining or improving EM by 1-7 points across all datasets
Good generalization properties: transfers across compressor architectures (Figure 3), downstream LLMs (Table 2), and generalizes from 5-doc to 10-doc without retraining
Thorough ablation studies demonstrating necessity of both distillation warm-start and GRPO components
Clear presentation with informative visualizations and case studies (Tables 4-5) showing qualitative improvements in summary quality
Practical value: compressor is 9-450x smaller than downstream LLM, reducing computational overhead while maintaining architecture agnosticism
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: primarily combines existing techniques (GRPO from Shao et al. 2024, standard distillation, QA metrics) without significant innovation in individual components

Misleading 'lossless' framing: claims lossless compression while reducing context from 712→46 tokens (94% reduction) that substantially changes information; more accurate to claim 'effective' or 'beneficial' compression

Insufficient analysis of training efficiency: no wall-clock training time, computational cost, or overhead analysis reported despite requiring downstream LLM inference for every RL rollout during training (5 rollouts × 256 batch size)

Distillation data filtering may introduce bias: uses DeepSeek-V3 supervision and filters examples based on teacher performance, with no analysis of retention rate or distribution shift; could bias toward DeepSeek-V3 summarization style

Reward design lacks justification and exploration: simple weighted sum of EM and F1 with dataset-dependent α hyperparameter (0.2-0.5); no exploration of alternative reward formulations or principled hyperparameter selection

Limited generalization scope: only evaluated on QA with defined answers, small-to-medium LLMs (8-14B), and transfer only to one alternative LLM; unclear if method generalizes to large LLMs or open-ended tasks

Incomplete analysis of learned behavior: beyond two case studies, no systematic investigation of compression patterns, failure modes, or performance across different document types and question complexities
Unfair DeepSeek-V3 comparison: DeepSeek-V3 wasn't task-specifically trained for compression like CORE, making direct performance comparison conflate RL optimization benefits with method superiority

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing practical RAG efficiency concerns with clear empirical demonstration of the issue
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 4 datasets with extensive ablations, hyperparameter studies, and robust baseline comparisons
Exceptional generalization results: transfers to longer contexts (5→10 docs), different LLMs (Qwen→Llama), different datasets, and different compressor architectures without retraining
Sound technical approach combining knowledge distillation for warm-start initialization with GRPO-based performance-driven optimization
Practical and efficient design: lightweight compressor module that is easy to deploy with significant computational savings
Clear and well-organized presentation with informative figures and thorough case studies illustrating compression quality
Strong empirical results: achieves 3-6% context compression while matching or improving performance over full-context RAG across all datasets
Good reproducibility: detailed implementation details, hyperparameters, training time, and promised code release
weaknesses: Limited novelty: straightforward application of existing techniques (distillation + GRPO) rather than novel methodological contributions
Insufficient explanation of core phenomenon: paper doesn't adequately explain why compression can improve performance over full-context RAG, missing opportunity for deeper insights
Narrow scope: evaluation limited to extractive QA tasks with only speculative discussion of open-ended settings and no empirical validation
Distillation dependency: heavy reliance on DeepSeek-V3 as teacher without ablation on teacher quality or exploration of alternative teachers

Unclear training data methodology: paper doesn't clearly specify if RL phase reuses filtered examples from distillation (potential overfitting) or uses fresh examples; filtering statistics not reported
Missing statistical rigor: no error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests despite some improvements being modest (1-2 EM points)
Insufficient hyperparameter analysis: only α studied in detail; sensitivity to other hyperparameters (β, learning rate, G) not explored
Limited failure analysis: case studies show successes but lack investigation of failure modes, systematic errors, or when the method underperforms
Incomplete generalization experiments: length generalization only tested on 5→10 documents; other lengths and generalization patterns not explored
Arbitrary design choices: 2-sentence summary constraint not justified; no sensitivity analysis for prompt template variations
Narrow noise robustness evaluation: only tested on NQ with random document noise; real-world noise patterns and other datasets not comprehensively evaluated
Baseline comparison concerns: DeepSeek-V3 generates 50-92 tokens vs CORE's 32-49, complicating performance comparison; fairness of comparisons with different summary lengths
Incomplete discussion of computational costs: distillation phase using 671B model computationally expensive but cost not thoroughly analyzed
